args.note: Analysis is written. Young Americans Center: partly. Bill Reynolds: partly. Smells like school: yes, 5 pages (p31, 47, 59, 60, 61; p59 and p61 are whole pages that explain). The book does not leave a reader thinking free enterprise is bad: p44, 61 and 63 end on a licensed sale, property left untouched and an agreed repair price. Main problems: the 10-page prologue goes nowhere; Bi11bot asks questions but doesn't talk like Bill; nothing on the page explains the debt mechanics, the 104k drop or the neighbours' 500 credits; and Alex never fails himself and faces the person he owes.
